analysis.title: Can I get that without AI? Wall Street's new favorite trade
key_insights: The Goldman broad-based AI basket fell 20% over five sessions, toward the lower end of recent unwind episodes (GS trading desk, Marquee).
SOX fell for an eighth straight trading day, its first eight-day slide since September 2015. It fell nine sessions in May 2006. The ETF is down more than 15% over the stretch.
Systematic multi-strat funds had a 2.2 sigma negative performance day, but are still up 20% YTD (GS Prime).

NDX forward P/E is back to about 21x, the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023. The NDX is testing its trendline from the March lows. Callahan suggests this could support earnings season, where earnings (the 'E') could do some work.

Two fundamental concerns are named: credit market stress in AI data center high-yield debt, and China hardware exports running about 36% above a year ago, which threatens the US hardware bottleneck thesis.
Investors are looking for opportunities outside AI. The correlation between AI and SPXXAI is falling again.

The GS trading desk likes buying SPXXAI as an entry point to rotate into the broader non-AI market, and expects the dispersion to narrow as AI headline risk (financing costs, hardware demand, capex discipline) catches up with equity pricing.
Data center capex estimates for 2027 continue to rise despite higher rates (Apollo).
AI-linked financing costs are not excessive relative to the rest of the credit stack, though the gap opens up further out the curve.
